title: Strategic Plan approved; farmland and heritage demolitions addressed
subtitle: Tax rates, St. David Street reconstruction, animal control contract, community grants, committee appointments, and cannabis and disc golf reports.
overview: Council approved the 2023 to 2026 Strategic Plan {{vote:m4}}, with an added requirement for an internal review and refresh before the 2025 budget process. Staff will also prepare an annual Corporate Business Plan starting with the 2024 budget, and a new advisory committee structure was approved.

Council authorized comments on the proposed Provincial Planning Statement and will send a letter opposing up to three additional residential units on agricultural land {{vote:m6}}. Council approved demolitions at listed heritage properties in Elora, which stay on the Municipal Heritage Register {{vote:m7}} {{vote:m8}}.

On spending, Council approved Community Impact Grants totalling $159,428 {{vote:m10}}, a Connecting Links agreement and design contract for St. David Street North in Fergus {{vote:m12}}, and a new animal control contract with the Guelph Humane Society {{vote:m18}}. Council also set 2023 tax rates {{vote:m14}} and adopted an updated reserve policy {{vote:m15}}. Staff will report on a disc golf course {{vote:m28}} and on opting into the provincial cannabis retail program {{vote:m29}}.

decisions.detail: Council approved the plan, an annual Corporate Business Plan from the 2024 budget, the advisory committee structure, and a review and refresh before the 2025 budget {{vote:m4}}.
Council authorized staff comments and a letter opposing up to three additional residential units on agricultural land, to be circulated to Wellington County municipalities {{vote:m6}}.

decisions.item: Elora demolitions on Geddes, Princess and Moir streets
decisions.detail: Council approved demolition of a detached garage and the Elora Cafe and Kitras Glass building, with the properties staying on the Municipal Heritage Register {{vote:m7}}.

Council authorized a Connecting Links agreement with the province, a single-source design contract to Triton Engineering Services Limited up to $485,900, and a reserve transfer of up to $15,250 {{vote:m12}}.
Council approved grant allocations totalling $159,428 as recommended by staff {{vote:m10}}.
Council awarded the contract to the Guelph Humane Society for an initial 18-month term up to $398,262, with renewals for three additional one-year terms {{vote:m18}}.
Council adopted the updated policy and approved the recommended transfers between reserves as at December 31, 2022 {{vote:m15}}.
Council approved demolition of the Walser Building Ruin at 6523 Wellington Road 7, which stays on the Municipal Heritage Register {{vote:m8}}.
